deep.reconstruction:
This page sets up the geometry for a computation of the arithmetic/'mixed' fundamental group of the projective line minus three points, U = U_{0,3} = P^1(C) - {0,1,∞}, which is identical to M_{0,4}.

(1) Base point. Grothendieck takes P to be one of the two fixed points of the order-3 Möbius map ρ(z) = 1/(1-z), namely P, P̄ = e^{±iπ/3}, the roots of z^2 - z + 1 = 0. He writes π = π_{0,3} = π_1(U, P), a free group on two generators.

(2) Metric. The sphere gets the round metric invariant under the symmetry group of the configuration. In it:
- P and P̄ are antipodal poles.
- 0, 1, ∞ are equally spaced on the equator, which is the real circle.
- ρ is rotation by +2π/3 about the axis PP̄ and induces the cycle 0→1→∞→0. This matches the usual orientation.

(3) Symmetries. The three anharmonic involutions are half-turns of the sphere:
- σ_0(z) = z/(z-1), axis (0,2);
- σ_1(z) = 1/z, axis (1,-1);
- σ_∞(z) = 1-z, axis (∞,1/2).
Complex conjugation τ is reflection in the plane through 0, 1, ∞. The margin also records ρ^2(z) = 1 - 1/z. Altogether Γ = S_3 × Z/2 (order 12, the full symmetry group D_{3h} of the bipyramid on P, P̄, 0, 1, ∞) acts on U. The S_3 part is holomorphic; τ is antiholomorphic.

(4) The extension. He defines the 'mixed' or equivariant fundamental group E = E_{0,3} = π_1(U, Γ; P), an extension 1 → π → E → Γ → 1. The next page makes this explicit: E consists of pairs (γ, ℓ) with γ in Γ and ℓ a path class from P to γ^{-1}(P), with the twisted composition law.

Purpose. The surrounding pages aim at an explicit presentation of E, and of its profinite analogue, through generators l_i (loops), σ_i (lifts of the transpositions, using paths along half great circles fixed by τσ_i) and ε_i. This is the first stage of the 'Teichmüller tower / lego' and of the Galois action on π̂_1 of P^1 - {0,1,∞} (La Longue Marche, spring 1981). The S_3 lifts and the order-3 base point are exactly where the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations later codified in Drinfeld's GT originate.

What E is, in modern terms (not stated on the page). E is the orbifold fundamental group of [U/Γ]:
- U/S_3 is the j-line with orbifold points of orders 3 and 2, so π_1^orb([U/S_3]) = Z/3 * Z/2 = PSL_2(Z), and π corresponds to Γ(2)/±1.
- Adding τ gives E ≅ PGL_2(Z), the extended (2,3,∞) triangle reflection group.
Equivalently, since π has trivial centre, E is the group of peripheral-structure-preserving automorphisms of F_2, i.e. the extended mapping class group of the sphere with 3 unordered punctures and a marked point.
errors: 'Structure riemannienne usuelle' is loose. The standard Fubini-Study metric in the coordinate z does not make 1-z or z/(z-1) isometries. The intended metric is the Γ-invariant round metric with P, P̄ as poles (the standard metric transported by a Möbius map). With that reading, all axes stated are correct: fixed points of z/(z-1) are 0, 2; of 1/z are ±1; of 1-z are 1/2, ∞.
Marginal formulas are all correct: σ_0 fixes 0 and swaps 1, ∞; σ_1 fixes 1 and swaps 0, ∞; σ_∞ fixes ∞ and swaps 0, 1; ρ gives 0→1→∞→0; ρ^2 = 1 - 1/z.

Related to the previous page, not this one. The relation 'σ_∞ σ_1 σ_0 = 1' derived there cannot hold if the σ_i are lifts in E of the three transpositions: the image in S_3 is a product of three transpositions, which is odd and so not 1. This is consistent with Grothendieck's own 'Critique des relations et de l'approche' and the fresh start on this page.

ideas.what: Base point chosen at the order-3 fixed point e^{iπ/3}, with the Γ-invariant round metric making all symmetries isometries.
ideas.modern_name: Symmetric (non-tangential) base point for π_1(P^1 - {0,1,∞}); compare Ihara's and Deligne's tangential base points.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tangential base points: Deligne (1989), Ihara. Symmetric-point choices: Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura (1990s).
ideas.where_published: Likely in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated; partial transcription by Malgoire).

ideas.what: Realisation of the anharmonic group S_3 and complex conjugation as the isometry group S_3 × Z/2 of the sphere: half-turns about the axes (0,2), (1,-1), (∞,1/2) and reflection in the real plane.
Equivariant ('mixed') fundamental group π_1(U, Γ; P) as an extension of Γ by π_1(U, P), where Γ acts with fixed points and includes the antiholomorphic τ.
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold / stack fundamental group of [U/Γ]. Here it is ≅ PGL_2(Z), the extended (2,3,∞) triangle group.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Orbifold π_1: Thurston (1978). Equivariant fundamental groupoid: R. Brown, Higgins and others. Topos-theoretic π_1: Grothendieck (SGA).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses Teichmüller groups and Galois action on the tower but not this exact notation; La Longue Marche (1981) likely contains it.

ideas.what: Programme of presenting E (and its profinite completion) via lifts σ_i of transpositions and an order-3 lift, preparing the Galois action on the genus-0 Teichmüller tower.
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck-Teichmüller theory; the 2- and 3-cycle relations of GT.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s); Grothendieck programmatically in the Esquisse.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §2 (Teichmüller tower, lego); La Longue Marche (1981).

missed.claim: Fine detail of how Grothendieck set up the symmetric base point and the mixed group E_{0,3}, including complex conjugation inside Γ. This is the 1981 precursor of the GT relations. It is likely documented in La Longue Marche, so the only novelty is archival detail. The page never notes that E ≅ PGL_2(Z), a classical identification.
missed.quote: On considère l'extension E_{0,3} de S_3 × Z/2 par π, notée E, définie par E = π_1(U_{0,3}, S_3 × Z/2; P)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: shows the order-3 symmetric base point and the antiholomorphic symmetry built into the 'mixed' group from the outset, close to later treatments of GT with complex conjugation (Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura). Not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: Set-up page: classical anharmonic symmetries and an equivariant fundamental group which is classically PGL_2(Z). Interesting historically as part of the Longue Marche / Teichmüller-tower programme, but the ideas are known and largely documented.
transcription_corrections: 'c'est la symétrie par un plan [...]. On considère...' should read 'c'est la symétrie par le plan (0,1,∞). On considère S_3 comme opérant sur (0,1,∞) dans cet ordre...'. The '(0,1,∞)' begins the next line and names the plane.
Margin: σ_0(z) is written as -z/(1-z) = z/(z-1); the '[?]' can be removed.
Under the displayed formula for E, 'U_{0,3}' is written below U as an alternative label, matching 'E_{0,3} ou' added above E.
